newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Anhui Expressway seen too risky for some.
newsitem.headline: Anhui Expressway seen too risky for some.

text.p: Anhui Expressway Co Ltd's market debut on Wednesday could be a drab affair with the Chinese toll operator's reliance on a sole expressway likely to make its initial public offering (IPO) too risky for some investors, analysts said on Monday.
The company offered a total 493.01 million H-shares at HK$1.77 per share, of which 73.95 million were offered in an IPO in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong IPO was 1.04 times subscribed.
"Its fundamentals are not that exciting because its earnings growth depends very much on a single road," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
Anhui Expressway owns, operates and develops toll roads in China's inner Anhui province. It currently owns and operates the 134-km Hening (Nefei-Nanjing) Expressway.
"Future prospects will depend on whether it can buy more roads to strengthen its earnings base," said Kwong.

Anhui Expressway said proceeds of the offering would be used to fund its purchase of the Tianchang section of National Highway 205 and to fund the purchase, installation and upgrading of a new toll collection system and traffic monitoring system on the Hening Expressway.
Proceeds will also be used to repay loans and for future acquisitions of other prospective highway projects, it said.
Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment Strategy, said the low subscription rate for the offering was likely to mean an unexciting debut.
"Its debut is unlikely to draw much attention as the market does not seem to be interested in the H-share sector, particularly since it is an operator of just one toll road in China," he said.
Anhui Expressway is the 22nd Chinese enterprise to list H-shares in Hong Kong. H-shares are shares of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
Analysts said there were other infrastructure stocks already in the market which were deemed more attractive and other upcoming issues which investors may choose to favour.
Bus operator Citybus Group Ltd and data storage products maker Jackin International Holdings Ltd are expected to kick off their IPOs later this week, analysts said.
